channel.title: Digiwaxx University
channel.description: Guides, straight answers and campaign playbooks on DJ promotion, radio, playlists and breaking records, from the record pool that has served working DJs since 1998.

item.title: The Data Trail DJs Leave: Spins, Crates, Charts and What They Tell You
item.description: Record pool downloads, detected spins and DJ charts are the earliest data in music. How each layer works and how to read a campaign report.
item.dc:creator: Kay Ali

item.title: Streaming Numbers Lie, Rooms Don’t: The Music Metrics That Actually Matter
item.description: The effort test: metrics a listener has to earn, saves, searches, Shazams, repeat spins, beat any number that can be bought. Here is why.
item.dc:creator: Kay Ali

item.title: Mixshow vs. Rotation: How Radio Airplay Really Works
item.description: The two-tier radio system nobody explains to artists: what a mixshow is, how spins get counted, and how records graduate to rotation.
item.dc:creator: Kay Ali

item.title: How to Release African Music to U.S. DJs: Clean Versions, DJ Edits and EPK Requirements
item.description: The unglamorous checklist that decides whether American DJs can actually play your record. Most campaigns that fail, fail here.

item.title: How Songs Break City by City: Viral Charts, Shazam Maps and Local Heat
item.description: Charts are national but breakouts are local. How viral and city charts work, and why the ignition point is almost always a DJ booth.
item.dc:creator: Kay Ali

item.title: How Shazam Works for Artists: From the Club Floor to the Charts
item.description: A Shazam is a stranger hunting down your record seconds after a DJ played it. Why that makes it one of the most honest demand signals in music.
item.dc:creator: Kay Ali

item.title: How Nigerian Artists Can Promote Afrobeats to DJs in the United States
item.description: The streams say Nigeria already won. The rooms are the part you still have to work, and the rooms belong to DJs. A practical guide.

item.title: From Lagos and Accra to New York, Atlanta and London: A DJ Promotion Plan
item.description: A six week servicing plan for taking an African release into the diaspora cities, in the order the rooms actually work.

item.title: Amapiano Promotion in the U.S.: DJs, Clubs, Mixshows and Diaspora Audiences
item.description: A format born in the DJ booth breaks abroad through DJ booths. How a South African release actually reaches American floors.

item.title: Afrobeats vs. Amapiano Promotion: Different DJ Campaigns for Different Markets
item.description: One is a song format, one is a set format, and a campaign that treats them the same will underserve both.

item.title: Afrobeats DJ Promotion: What Labels Need for U.S. DJ Servicing
item.description: A checklist for the label side of a U.S. Afrobeats campaign: what to prepare, what a servicing partner should do, and what to refuse to pay for.

item.title: “I’m Getting Traction.”: Converting Momentum Into a Career
item.description: The record is moving, now convert: bookings, complete royalty collection, publishing, performance rights, sync, and the next-release flywheel.

item.title: “I Released It… and Nothing Happened.”
item.description: No streams, no saves, no playlist adds after release? Why silence is the default for unpromoted records, and the exact recovery plan.

item.title: “I Need People.”: Building Your Amplification Network
item.description: The people layer of music promotion: DJs, radio, playlist curators, blogs, and influencers, what each one does, in what order, and how to reach them.

item.title: “I Made a Song.”: Now What?
item.description: You finished a song. The exact next steps: mastering, versions, artwork, metadata, ISRC, distribution, and lining up the people who will play it.

item.title: YouTube Music Promotion
item.description: How to promote music on YouTube: the second-biggest search engine, Shorts as a discovery engine, visualizers vs. videos, and converting views into streams and fans.

item.title: Will Promotion Increase My Streams?
item.description: How real promotion converts to streams: exposure → searches and saves → algorithmic pickup. What to expect, what not to, and why bought streams destroy the loop.

item.title: Why Your Song Stopped Growing
item.description: Streams flatlined after a good start? The four reasons songs plateau and the second-wave playbook for restarting momentum without re-uploading.

item.title: Why Nobody Listens to Your Music (Yet)
item.description: The honest reasons nobody is listening to your music yet, exposure math, trust signals, and the fixable gap between good songs and heard songs.

item.title: What to Do the Day Your Song Drops
item.description: Hour-by-hour release day checklist for independent artists: verification, links, content, outreach, and what to do that night.

item.title: What Is a Record Pool?
item.description: Record pool, defined: a membership service distributing new music to verified working DJs, its 1970s origins, how it went digital, and its role in breaking records.

item.title: What Happens After You Submit Music to a Record Pool
item.description: The step-by-step of what happens after submission: review, packaging, servicing to the DJ network, pickup, spins, and the feedback that comes back to you.

item.title: Tidal Promotion
item.description: How to promote music on Tidal: higher payouts, editorial playlists, Tidal Rising for emerging artists, and where Tidal fits in an independent release strategy.

item.title: The Song Rollout Timeline
item.description: A week-by-week rollout timeline for an independent single: what happens at 6 weeks out, 4 weeks, 2 weeks, release week, and after.

item.title: The Music Marketing Checklist
item.description: The complete music marketing checklist for independent artists, assets, profiles, pre-release, DJ service, release week, and post-release, in one list.
